_meta: AF/G.23 (2026-08-13), continuing systematic Africa-branch municipal-fiscal-tier research. Seychelles was previously researched in AF/G.17 (see af-seychelles.json), which concluded a genuine structural absence (26 districts, no independent fiscal tier) based on secondary/academic sources only. This round obtained two new raw-verified primary documents that substantially strengthen that conclusion without overturning it: (1) a directly-extracted verbatim quote of Constitution Article 167 (a bare administrative-division enabling clause, no fiscal-autonomy language), and (2) the Ministry of Finance's 2026 Budget Estimates, which itemizes the Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands' (MLGII) finances line-by-line and explicitly shows districts are financed 100% from the central Consolidated Fund, with even minor locally-collected receipts (burial fees, facility rentals) remitted back to the centre rather than retained. Both are minted as new nodes here; no district/municipal-tier node is minted, since none exists to document (structural absence, not a research gap). The Auditor-General's report-PDF content and a possible Victoria 'Capital City' charter/Act remain unresolved leads for a future round (see _dropped).

reports.title: Constitution of the Republic of Seychelles — Article 167 (Local Administration)
reports.description: Chapter XV ("Miscellaneous"), Article 167 ("Local Administration") of the Constitution of the Republic of Seychelles — the sole constitutional provision touching sub-national administration. Verbatim text (directly extracted from a raw-downloaded PDF, not a secondary paraphrase): "167.(1) A law may, for the purpose of facilitating the administrative functions of the State in respect of its social and economic undertakings contained in Chapter III, provide for the division of Seychelles into such number of units which shall bear such name as the law may specify. (2) A law referred to in clause (1) may provide for the composition and the functions of the units and for all other matters necessary to give effect to the provisions of that clause." This wording was independently cross-checked against a second, separately-hosted copy (constituteproject.org's PDF) and found substantively identical. Article 167 is a bare permissive/enabling clause for *administrative* division only ("administrative functions of the State") — it contains no reference to elected local government, revenue-raising power, or fiscal autonomy, corroborating from the primary constitutional text itself that no constitutionally-mandated local fiscal tier exists. No enabling Act implementing this clause was located in the National Assembly's Acts listing this round (search returned "No results found"), consistent with this branch's prior finding that the 1991 Local Government Act was suspended in 1993 and never re-enacted. ACCESS CAVEAT: the government's own domain for this text (gov.sc) and the Seychelles Legal Information Institute (seylii.org / old.seylii.org) were both bot/captcha-gated (`robocop` CAPTCHA) this round; this URL is a third-party intergovernmental mirror (ARIPO, the African Regional Intellectual Property Organization), not a Seychelles-government-controlled domain, though the text itself is independently cross-verified.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational legal instrument (constitutional text, in force; text unchanged across consolidations checked).

reports.title: 2026 Budget Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure for the Fiscal Year Ended 31st December 2026 — Part 1 (Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands chapter)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Economic Planning, Trade and Investment, Republic of Seychelles
reports.description: Republic of Seychelles national budget document; the Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands (MLGII) chapter (printed pages ~411-416, plus a Public Sector Investment Programme annex) is the strongest primary evidence yet obtained in this branch's Seychelles research for the country's district administration having no independent fiscal tier. Table 1 ("Revenue") for MLGII: "Consolidated Fund 135,378 168,999 164,212 166,448 169,611 157,371 / Main appropriation 135,378 168,999 164,212 166,448 169,611 157,371 / Total 135,378 168,999 164,212 166,448 169,611 157,371" [SR'000s, 2024 Actual through 2028 Forecast] — i.e. 100% of MLGII's SR166,448,000 2026 appropriation is drawn from the general Consolidated Fund, not district-specific or district-raised revenue. Table 2 ("Current receipts") shows the ONLY revenue MLGII/district offices collect locally is captioned "Receipts transferred to Consolidated Fund": "Burial Services Fees 191 205 205 205 205 205 / Rent of facilities 1,801 1,700 1,700 1,700 1,700 1,700 / Rent of Offices 348 500 500 400 400 400 / Rent of Day-care centres 1,065 1,080 1,080 1,200 1,200 1,200 / TOTAL 3,405 3,485 3,485 3,505 3,505 3,505" [SR'000s] — even this minor local collection (roughly 2% of the Ministry's budget) is remitted back to the centre, not retained by district administration. The Ministry's own stated mandate: "The mandate of the Ministry of Local Government and Inner Islands (MLGII) is to oversee the affairs of the districts and to empower the local communities... as well as maintaining linkages between the central and local government" — i.e. a national ministry overseeing districts, not districts self-governing. The consolidated "SP1: District Administration" sub-programme line (SR96,291,000 in the 2026 budget, covering all 26 districts/27 District Administration Offices nationally) is not broken down per district in the summary tables, but the PSIP annex DOES itemize named-district capital projects (e.g. Cascade Community Centre, Les Mamelles Day Care Centre, Ile Perseverance 1 DA's Office, Grand Anse Praslin Day Care, Anse Aux Pins Day Care, Takamaka Day Care, Glacis Day Care, Baie St Anne Community Centre/DA's Office (La Digue), Belombre DA's Office, Au Cap Community Centre, Baie Lazare Community Centre, Anse Royale Community Centre), each financed by "GOS" (Government of Seychelles) or "GOI" (Government of India, a foreign grant/loan) codes — never a district-level or locally-raised funding source, reinforcing that districts are named capital-allocation *recipients*, not independent budget-holders. ACCESS CAVEAT: this is a large (approximately 8MB, 799-page) PDF; the WebFetch tool returned a 504 proxy timeout attempting to summarize it, and the text quoted here was obtained only by downloading the file directly with curl and extracting it with pdftotext — flagged per protocol as a large-PDF/technical-access caveat, though the resulting quotes are raw-verified, not AI-summarized.
reports.cadence_note: Annual national budget estimates; this is the 2026 edition (forecasts extend to 2028).

_dropped.why: The 2026 Budget's MLGII chapter and the Ministry's own website both cite Article 167 as their constitutional authority (per the AI-summarized-only Ministry website finding, Finding 6 in this round's raw research: "Article 167 of the Constitution of the Third Republic of Seychelles"), but the budget document ITSELF (the raw-verified PDF) does not contain a citing sentence naming Article 167 — the citation only appears on the captcha-gated, AI-summarized-only Ministry website. Not minted as a live dependency edge given the weaker sourcing tier for the citing statement; recorded here as a note rather than force-linked.

The Office of the Auditor General of Seychelles (oag.sc / oag.sc/reports/annual-reports-of-the-auditor-general) publishes annual reports back to 2011 (e.g. "Report of the Auditor General 2024", "Annual Report 2023") and is exactly the 'higher tier of government reporting on named lower-tier units' document type productive elsewhere in this branch (e.g. Nigeria). This round reached only the report LISTING (titles/dates), not the content of any individual report PDF — direct curl is blocked by an `sg-captcha` bot-protection gate on oag.sc, and WebFetch could not follow through to a specific report's PDF text (likely JS-rendered pagination). No node minted since no content was verified. Genuine unresolved lead for a future round, not a confirmed absence.

A currently-operating 'Mayor of Victoria' office was confirmed to exist (mayorsofficeseychelles.com; current mayor named as Mrs. Michaud-Payet, office at Revolution Avenue, Victoria) but no enabling Act, legal charter, or budget/fiscal document establishing a 'Victoria City Council' or 'Borough of Victoria' was located this round; the office's own site is described as promotional/informational only with no governance-structure documentation. victoria.gov.sc returned HTTP 421 (Misdirected Request) with no retrievable content. Appears to be a ceremonial/civic-engagement office rather than a fiscally autonomous municipal government, but this could not be confirmed either way with a primary legal document. Not minted as a node; flagged as an open lead for a future round (a WebSearch for a 'Victoria (Capital City) Act' was queued but not executed this round due to search-budget exhaustion).

UPDATE 2026-08-13 (AF/G.23): the existing af-seychelles.json _dropped note documenting Seychelles's structural absence of an independent local-fiscal-tier (sourced there only from secondary/academic documents — University of Pretoria report, CLGF profile) is now substantially strengthened by two raw-verified primary documents minted in this file: sc-constitution-article-167 (verbatim Article 167 text, confirming the constitutional provision is a bare administrative-division enabling clause with no fiscal-autonomy language) and sc-mlgii-budget-2026 (the Ministry of Finance's 2026 Budget, directly showing 100% Consolidated-Fund financing of district administration with even minor local receipts remitted back to the centre). This remains recorded as 'note' (not 'resolved') because it documents a structural absence rather than a live dependency edge between two corpus nodes.
